spec.title: Billakanti and Shin, "At-Risk Transformation for U.S. Recession Prediction" (International Journal of Forecasting, conditionally accepted): first Linux run
spec.paper: Rahul Billakanti and Minchul Shin, At-Risk Transformation for U.S. Recession Prediction, International Journal of Forecasting, conditionally accepted
spec.cost_basis: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner, free for public repositories (a comparable 4 vCPU cloud machine is about 0.20 USD an hour)

environment_commands.cmd: uv --version; pdftoppm -v 2>&1 | head -1; nproc; free -g | head -2; program_v04/.venv/bin/python -c 'import sys,numpy,sklearn,xgboost;print(sys.version);print(numpy.__version__,sklearn.__version__,xgboost.__version__)' || true

setup.cmd: python -m pip install --quiet uv && sudo apt-get install -y -q poppler-utils >/dev/null && uv --version
cd program_v04 && uv sync --locked && cd .. && uv pip install --python program_v04/.venv/bin/python xlrd==2.0.2

commands.cmd: python3 scripts/run_replication.py; rc=$?; echo '--- run_report.json'; cat run_report.json 2>/dev/null; exit $rc

scope_notes: The README's full run: every model estimated from the 308 public inputs, then the package's own comparison of 50 outputs with the manuscript references, at its own tolerance; the log holds its output.
The tested platform is macOS on Apple Silicon. This is an x86-64 Linux runner, so the run also says whether the results carry across platforms.
